source.title: CPR: Classifier-Projection Regularization for Continual Learning
source.authors: Sung-Min Cha; Hsiang Hsu; Taebaek Hwang; F. Calmon; Taesup Moon

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; some plotted values are not numerically recoverable from the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses wide-local-minimum regularization to improve continual learning and reports its method’s performance. Its perturbation experiments measure local-minimum width, but do not test the claim versions’ natural-label generalization gap or magnitude-aware sharpness relationship.
record.gate_note: The paper cites batch size and other wide-minimum work as prior research; those cited results are not rows. Its own continual-learning accuracy, forgetting, and intransigence comparisons do not measure the claim versions. Rows below capture its own perturbation and loss-landscape measurements as related findings outside the versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses wide-minimum regularization to improve continual learning. Its own results measure accuracy, forgetting, plasticity and perturbation tolerance, but do not test any listed version. In particular, V7 requires magnitude-aware weight perturbations related to training–test gaps; neither is measured here.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' central conclusion: CPR promotes wider local minima and improves continual-learning accuracy, stability and plasticity. This describes their overall conclusion, not uniform improvement of every metric: supplementary Table 6 reports increased forgetting for LwF and HAT and increased intransigence for UCL.
record.recipe_differences: Adds classifier-output KL regularization to continual-learning methods; it does not test the original claim’s generalization-gap interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: CPR effects vary with β and task order; the authors report a stability-plasticity trade-off for MAS as β changes and note that CIFAR-10 task placement changes the CPR gain.

fits_no_version.finding: For EWC and MAS on sequential CIFAR-100 tasks, CPR produces slower or smoother loss growth under the reported Gaussian perturbations. EWC with CPR also has wider training-loss landscapes. These are qualitative method comparisons without magnitude-aware sharpness or training–test-gap measurements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CPR increases local perturbation tolerance and broadens loss landscapes in the tested continual-learning models.

record.problems: Perturbation and landscape results are figure-only, with no numerical estimates or uncertainty reported for those comparisons. The study does not measure training-test gaps or test the listed claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the paper’s continual-learning benchmark accuracy, forgetting, intransigence, reinforcement-learning rewards, or feature-map visualizations: these concern continual-learning performance or representations, not the claim versions’ specified measures. Cited prior-work results were also excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the contrast with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Held-out effects of adding, varying or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts apply to V1–V8. Adam and dropout occur in the training recipe without relevant controlled comparisons; batch-size findings are cited prior work. Qualitative perturbation and landscape differences are stated explicitly, even though exact plotted values are unavailable. The row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: EWC
rows.stage_stated: continual learning; trained through the final task
rows.operation_detail: Added Gaussian noise to parameters after the final task and measured test-loss increase for each task.
rows.note: The text describes the comparison with EWC+CPR, but provides no numerical values.
rows.check: Method comparator outside the claim versions. Section 3.2 describes test loss, but Figure 3(b)'s extracted axis says training loss; flag this inconsistency rather than treating the measure as unambiguous.

rows.subject: EWC + CPR
rows.stage_stated: continual learning; trained through the final task
rows.operation_detail: Added Gaussian noise to parameters after the final task and measured test-loss increase for each task.
rows.note: The authors state that test loss increases more smoothly than for EWC in each task; this does not measure the claim’s train-test gap.
rows.check: The study's own method comparison belongs under fits_no_version. The prose establishes smoother loss growth with CPR, but no V7 effect. Section 3.2 calls this test loss while the extracted figure axis says training loss.

rows.subject: EWC
rows.stage_stated: continual learning; trained through the final task
rows.operation_detail: Added Gaussian noise to test data and measured test-loss response.
rows.note: The figure compares EWC with EWC+CPR; values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: The operation is unsupported: supplementary Section 3.1 repeats the Section 3.2 experiment using test data, but does not explicitly say noise was added to inputs. Its caption is ambiguous. Do not confidently classify this as input-noise robustness.

rows.check: The study's method comparison belongs under fits_no_version. Slower test-loss growth is stated, but the assertion that noise was added to test inputs is not established; supplementary Section 3.1 refers back to the parameter-perturbation experiment.

rows.subject: EWC
rows.operation_detail: Visualized the training loss landscape across the first and second Hessian eigenvectors.
rows.note: Text states the EWC+CPR landscape is much wider than vanilla EWC; the measure does not establish a train-test-gap relationship.
rows.check: Training stage should be completion of all 10 tasks, with the landscape evaluated on task 2 training data. Supplementary Section 3.4 specifies that both models finished CIFAR-100 training. This method comparator does not measure V7.

rows.note: The paper says CPR makes the training loss landscape much wider; no numeric values are stated.
